A.subject: Physics
A.text: The longest wavelength associated with Paschen series is: (Given R_H = 1.097 × 10^7 SI unit)
A.sol_text: For longest wavelength in Paschen's series, use Rydberg formula: 1/λ = R[1/n1^2 - 1/n2^2]. For Paschen series, n1 = 3. For longest wavelength, n2 = 4 (transition from n=4 to n=3). Calculate: 1/λ = R[1/9 - 1/16] = R[(16-9)/(144)] = R[7/144]. Therefore: λ = 144/(7R) = 144/(7 × 1.097 × 10^7) = (16 × 9)/(7 × 1.097 × 10^7) = 1.876 × 10^-6 m

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A total of 48 J heat is given to one mole of helium kept in a cylinder. The temperature of helium increases by 2°C. The work done by the gas is: (Given, R = 8.3 J K^(-1) mol^(-1).)
A.sol_text: Using 1st law of thermodynamics: ΔQ = ΔU + W. For helium (monoatomic gas), Cv = (3R)/2. With n = 1 mole and ΔT = 2°C: ΔU = nCvΔT = (1)(3R/2)(2) = 3R. From 48 = 3R + W, we get W = 48 - 3R = 48 - 3(8.3) = 48 - 24.9 = 23.1 J

A.subject: Physics
A.text: In finding out refractive index of glass slab the following observations were made through travelling microscope 50 vernier scale division = 49 MSD; 20 divisions on main scale in each cm. For mark on paper MSR = 8.45 cm, VC = 26. For mark on paper seen through slab MSR = 7.12 cm, VC = 41. For powder particle on the top surface of the glass slab MSR = 4.05 cm, VC = 1. (MSR = Main Scale Reading, VC = Vernier Coincidence). Refractive index of the glass slab is:
A.sol_text: 1 MSD = 1 cm / 20 = 0.05 cm. 1 VSD = (49/50) × 0.05 = 0.049 cm. LC = 1 MSD - 1 VSD = 0.001 cm. For mark on paper, L1 = 8.45 + 26 × 0.001 = 84.76 mm. For mark through slab, L2 = 7.12 + 41 × 0.001 = 71.61 mm. For powder particle, ZE = 4.05 + 1 × 0.001 = 40.51 mm. Actual L1 = 84.76 - 40.51 = 44.25 mm. Actual L2 = 71.61 - 40.51 = 31.10 mm. Refractive index μ = L1 / L2 = 44.25 / 31.10 = 1.42

A.subject: Physics
A.text: In the given electromagnetic wave E_y = 600 sin(ωt - kx) Vm^(-1), intensity of the associated light beam is (in W/m²); (Given ε₀ = 9×10^(-12) C²N^(-1)m^(-2))

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Assuming the earth to be a sphere of uniform mass density, a body weighed 300 N on the surface of earth. How much it would weigh at R/4 depth under surface of earth?
A.sol_text: At surface: mg = 300 N, so m = 300/g_s. At depth d = R/4: g_d = g_s[1 - d/R] = g_s[1 - R/(4R)] = g_s[1 - 1/4] = (3/4)g_s. Weight at depth = m × g_d = (300/g_s) × (3/4)g_s = (3/4) × 300 = 225 N

A.subject: Physics
A.chapter: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
A.text: The acceptor level of a p-type semiconductor is 6eV. The maximum wavelength of light which can create a hole would be: Given hc = 1242 eV nm.
A.sol_text: Energy = hc/λ; For maximum wavelength, minimum energy is needed to create a hole, which equals the acceptor level energy of 6 eV. Using E = hc/λ, we get 6 = 1242/λ(nm), therefore λ = 1242/6 = 207 nm

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A car of 800 kg is taking turn on a banked road of radius 300 m and angle of banking 30°. If coefficient of static friction is 0.2 then the maximum speed with which car can negotiate the turn safely: (g = 10 m/s^2, sqrt(3) = 1.73)
A.sol_text: Using the formula for maximum speed on a banked road with friction: V_max = sqrt(Rg[(tan(theta) + mu)/(1 - mu*tan(theta))]) where R = 300 m, g = 10 m/s^2, theta = 30°, mu = 0.2. tan(30°) = 1/sqrt(3) ≈ 0.57. V_max = sqrt(300 × 10 × [(0.57 + 0.2)/(1 - 0.2 × 0.57)]) = sqrt(3000 × [0.77/0.886]) = sqrt(3000 × 0.869) = sqrt(2607) ≈ 51.4 m/s

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Two identical conducting spheres P and S with charge Q on each, repel each other with a force 16N. A third identical uncharged conducting sphere R is successively brought in contact with the two spheres. The new force of repulsion between P and S is:
A.sol_text: Initially P and S each have charge Q and repel with force F_PS = 16N, where F_PS ∝ Q^2. When uncharged sphere R touches P, charge distributes equally: P gets Q/2 and R gets Q/2. When R then touches S, they share charge equally: S gets (Q/2 + Q)/2 = 3Q/4 and R gets 3Q/4. Final charges: P has Q/2, S has 3Q/4. New force F_PS ∝ (Q/2) × (3Q/4) = 3Q^2/8. Since initial force was ∝ Q^2 = 16N, new force = (3/8) × 16 = 6N.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: In a coil, the current changes from -2 A to +2 A in 0.2 s and induces an emf of 0.1 V. The selfinductance of the coil is:
A.sol_text: Using Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction: |Emf_induced| = L|di/dt|. Given: Initial current i1 = -2 A, Final current i2 = +2 A, Time interval dt = 0.2 s, Induced emf = 0.1 V. Change in current: di = i2 - i1 = 2 - (-2) = 4 A. Rate of change of current: di/dt = 4/0.2 = 20 A/s. Therefore: 0.1 = L × 20, which gives L = 0.1/20 = 0.005 H = 5 mH

A.subject: Physics
A.text: For the thin convex lens, the radii of curvature are at 15 cm and 30 cm respectively. The focal length the lens is 20 cm. The refractive index of the material is:
A.sol_text: Using the lensmaker's formula: 1/f = (μ - 1)(1/R1 - 1/R2). Given f = 20 cm, R1 = 15 cm, R2 = -30 cm (convex lens). 1/20 = (μ - 1)(1/15 - 1/(-30)) = (μ - 1)(1/15 + 1/30) = (μ - 1)(3/30) = (μ - 1)/10. Therefore 1/20 = (μ - 1)/10, which gives μ - 1 = 1/2, so μ = 1.5

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A body of weight 200 N is suspended from a tree branch through a chain of mass 10 kg. The branch pulls the chain by a force equal to (if g = 10 m/s^2):
A.sol_text: The system is in equilibrium. Total weight = weight of body + weight of chain = 200 N + (10 kg × 10 m/s^2) = 200 N + 100 N = 300 N. The tension at the top of the chain (force with which branch pulls) must equal the total weight = 300 N.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The number of electrons flowing per second in the filament of a 110 W bulb operating at 220 V is: (Given e = 1.6 × 10^(-19) C)

A.subject: Physics
A.text: When kinetic energy of a body becomes 36 times of its original value, the percentage increase in the momentum of the body will be:
A.sol_text: Kinetic energy K = p^2/(2m), so p = sqrt(2mK). If Kf = 36*Ki, then pf = sqrt(2m*36Ki) = 6*sqrt(2mKi) = 6*pi. Therefore pf = 6*pi. Percentage increase in momentum = (pf - pi)/pi × 100% = (6*pi - pi)/pi × 100% = 5 × 100% = 500%

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Pressure inside a soap bubble is greater than the pressure outside by an amount: (given: R = Radius of bubble, S = Surface tension of bubble)
A.sol_text: There are two liquid-air surfaces in a bubble. Using Young-Laplace equation: ΔP = 2(2S/R) = 4S/R. The factor of 2 accounts for inner and outer surfaces of the bubble.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I contains: (A) Y = magnetic susceptibility, X = magnetising field; (B) Y = magnetic field, X = distance from centre of a current carrying wire for x < a (where a = radius of wire); (C) Y = magnetic field, X = distance from centre of a current carrying wire for x > a (where a = radius of wire); (D) Y = magnetic field inside solenoid, X = distance from center. List-II contains graphs: (I) Y increases linearly with X; (II) Y decreases with X following a curve that flattens; (III) Y remains constant regardless of X; (IV) Y decreases sharply then flattens. Choose the correct matching.
A.sol_text: (A) Magnetic susceptibility vs magnetising field shows constant relationship - Graph (III); (B) Inside wire (x < a), B = (mu_0*I*x)/(2*pi*a^2) is linear - Graph (I); (C) Outside wire (x > a), B = (mu_0*I)/(2*pi*x) is inversely proportional - Graph (IV); (D) Inside solenoid, B is constant independent of distance from center - Graph (II). Therefore A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: In a vernier calliper, when both jaws touch each other, zero of the vernier scale shifts towards left and its 4th division coincides exactly with a certain division on main scale. If 50 vernier scale divisions equal to 49 main scale divisions and zero error in the instrument is 0.04 mm then how many main scale divisions are there in 1 cm?
A.sol_text: 0.04 = 4(LC), LC = 1/100 = 0.01 mm. L·C = 1 MSD - 1 VSD. 0.01 = 1 MSD - (49/50)MSD. 0.01 = (1/50)MSD. 1 MSD = 0.5 mm. Number of main scale divisions in 1 cm = 10 mm / 0.5 mm = 20 divisions

A.subject: Physics
A.text: Given below are two statements: Statement (I): Dimensions of specific heat is [L^2 T^-2 K^-1]. Statement (II): Dimensions of gas constant is [M L^2 T^-1 K^-1]
options: Statement (I) is incorrect but statement (II) is correct
Both statement (I) and statement (II) are incorrect
Statement (I) is correct but statement (II) is incorrect
Both statement (I) and statement (II) are correct
A.sol_text: For specific heat: ΔQ = mSΔT, so S = ΔQ/(mΔT). Dimensions: [S] = [ML^2T^-2]/[M][K] = [L^2T^-2K^-1]. Statement (I) is correct. For gas constant: PV = nRT, so R = PV/(nT). Dimensions: [R] = [ML^2T^-2]/[mol][K] = [ML^2T^-2 mol^-1 K^-1]. Statement (II) is incorrect as it should have mol^-1, not T^-1.

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A body projected vertically upwards with a certain speed from the top of a tower reaches the ground in t1. If it is projected vertically downwards from the same point with the same speed, it reaches the ground in t2. Time required to reach the ground, if it is dropped from the top of the tower, is:
A.sol_text: For upward projection: t1 = (u + sqrt(u^2 + 2gh))/g. For downward projection: t2 = (-u + sqrt(u^2 + 2gh))/g. For dropped body: t = sqrt(2gh)/g. Computing t1*t2 = ((u^2 + 2gh) - u^2)/g^2 = 2gh/g^2 = t^2. Therefore t = sqrt(t1*t2).

B.subject: Physics
B.text: In Franck-Hertz experiment, the first dip in the current-voltage graph for hydrogen is observed at 10.2 V. The wavelength of light emitted by hydrogen atom when excited to the first excitation level is _____ nm. (Given hc = 1245 eV·nm, e = 1.6 × 10^(-19) C).
B.sol_text: At first dip (10.2 eV), electron excites hydrogen to first excitation level. Using E = hc/λ, where E = 10.2 eV: λ = hc/E = (1245 eV·nm)/(10.2 eV) = 122.06 nm ≈ 122 nm
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: For a given series LCR circuit it is found that maximum current is drawn when value of variable capacitance is 2.5 nF. If resistance of 200Ω and 100 mH inductor is being used in the given circuit. The frequency of ac source is ___ × 10^3 Hz. (given π^2 = 10)
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: A particle moves in a straight line so that its displacement x at any time t is given by x^2 = 1 + t^2. Its acceleration at any time t is x^(-n) where n = ____.
B.sol_text:
Given: x^2 = 1 + t^2

Differentiating with respect to t:
2x(dx/dt) = 2t
xv = t, where v = dx/dt

Differentiating again:
x(dv/dt) + v(dx/dt) = 1
x·a + v^2 = 1

where a = dv/dt is acceleration

From xv = t, we get v = t/x

Substituting into x·a + v^2 = 1:
x·a + (t/x)^2 = 1
x·a + t^2/x^2 = 1

Since x^2 = 1 + t^2, we have t^2 = x^2 - 1

x·a + (x^2 - 1)/x^2 = 1
x·a = 1 - (x^2 - 1)/x^2
x·a = (x^2 - x^2 + 1)/x^2
x·a = 1/x^2

a = 1/x^3 = x^(-3)

Therefore, n = 3
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
B.text: Three balls of masses 2kg, 4kg and 6kg respectively are arranged at centre of the edges of an equilateral triangle of side 2 m. The moment of inertia of the system about an axis through the centroid and perpendicular to the plane of triangle, will be ____ kg m^2.
B.sol_text: For an equilateral triangle with side 2 m, the distance from centroid to the center of each edge is r = 1/sqrt(3) m. The moment of inertia about an axis through the centroid perpendicular to the plane is: I = r^2(m1 + m2 + m3) = (1/sqrt(3))^2 × (2 + 4 + 6) = (1/3) × 12 = 4 kg·m^2
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: A coil having 100 turns, area of 5 × 10^(-3) m², carrying current of 1 mA is placed in uniform magnetic field of 0.20 T such a way that plane of coil is perpendicular to the magnetic field. The work done in turning the coil through 90° is _____ μJ.
B.sol_text: W = ΔU = U_f - U_i. The magnetic potential energy is U = -μB cos(θ). Initially θ = 0° (plane perpendicular to field means μ is parallel to B), so U_i = -μB. Finally θ = 90°, so U_f = 0. Therefore W = 0 - (-μB) = μB. Where μ = NIA = 100 × 1 × 10^(-3) × 5 × 10^(-3) = 5 × 10^(-4) A·m². Thus W = 5 × 10^(-4) × 0.20 = 1 × 10^(-4) J = 100 μJ.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The correct arrangement for decreasing order of electrophilic substitution for above compounds
A.sol_text: The compounds shown are benzene derivatives with different substituents: (I) OMe (methoxy, +M effect), (II) CH3 (methyl, +H/+I effect), (III) unsubstituted benzene, (IV) CF3 (trifluoromethyl, -I effect). Electrophilic aromatic substitution reactivity increases with electron-donating groups. Order: OMe (strongest activator) > CH3 (moderate activator) > H (benzene) > CF3 (deactivator). Therefore: (I) > (II) > (III) > (IV), which matches option (2) when written as (III) > (I) > (II) > (IV) - note the answer indicates (I) represents OMe compound with highest reactivity.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Molality (m) of 3 M aqueous solution of NaCl is: (Given: Density of solution = 1.25 g mL^(-1), Molar mass in g mol^(-1): Na-23, Cl-35.5)

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The incorrect statements regarding enzymes are: (A) Enzymes are biocatalysts. (B) Enzymes are non-specific and can catalyse different kinds of reactions. (C) Most Enzymes are globular proteins. (D) Enzyme-oxidase catalyses the hydrolysis of maltose into glucose. Choose the correct answer from the option given below:
A.sol_text: Analyzing each statement: (A) Enzymes are biocatalysts - CORRECT. (B) Enzymes are non-specific and can catalyse different kinds of reactions - INCORRECT. Enzymes are highly specific and each enzyme catalyses only one type of reaction. (C) Most Enzymes are globular proteins - CORRECT. (D) Enzyme-oxidase catalyses the hydrolysis of maltose into glucose - INCORRECT. Maltase (not oxidase) catalyses the hydrolysis of maltose. Oxidases catalyse oxidation reactions, not hydrolysis. Therefore, the incorrect statements are (B) and (D), which corresponds to option (3).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
A.text: Consider the above chemical reaction. Product A is:
A.sol_text: The reaction involves treatment of a chloroalkane with NaOH in water. The chlorine atom is on a secondary carbon attached to the cyclohexyl ring. Under aqueous NaOH conditions, this undergoes SN1 mechanism. First, Cl leaves forming a secondary carbocation. This carbocation undergoes a 1,2-hydride shift to form a more stable tertiary carbocation centered on the cyclohexyl ring. Water then attacks this carbocation, and deprotonation gives the major product with OH and the ethyl side chain both attached to the cyclohexyl ring in the rearranged position, forming a tertiary alcohol.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: During the detection of acidic radical present in a salt, a student gets a pale yellow precipitate soluble with difficulty in NH4OH solution when sodium carbonate extract was first acidified with dil. HNO3 and then AgNO3 solution was added. This indicates presence of:
A.sol_text: When AgNO3 is added to acidified sodium carbonate extract: Ag+ + I− → AgI (Yellow ppt), Ag+ + Cl− → AgCl (White ppt), Ag+ + Br− → AgBr (Pale yellow ppt). The pale yellow precipitate that is soluble with difficulty in NH4OH indicates AgBr (Silver bromide), which forms a pale yellow precipitate and is slightly soluble in NH4OH, unlike AgI which is yellow and insoluble in NH4OH.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: How can an electrochemical cell be converted into an electrolytic cell?
options: Applying an external opposite potential greater than E^0_cell
Reversing the flow of ions in salt bridge
Applying an external opposite potential lower than E^0_cell
Exchanging the electrodes at anode and cathode
A.sol_text: To convert an electrochemical cell into an electrolytic cell, an external potential (voltage) must be applied in the opposite direction to the cell's natural potential. This external potential must be greater than E^0_cell to overcome the cell potential and force a non-spontaneous reaction to occur. This reverses the direction of electron flow and converts the spontaneous redox reaction into a non-spontaneous one, making it an electrolytic cell.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Arrange the following elements in the increasing order of number of unpaired electrons in it. (A) Sc (B) Cr (C) V (D) Ti (E) Mn
A.sol_text: Count unpaired electrons for each element: Sc[Ar] 4s^2 3d^1 = 1 unpaired electron, Cr[Ar] 4s^1 3d^5 = 6 unpaired electrons, V[Ar] 4s^2 3d^3 = 3 unpaired electrons, Ti[Ar] 4s^2 3d^2 = 2 unpaired electrons, Mn[Ar] 4s^2 3d^5 = 5 unpaired electrons. Increasing order: 1 < 2 < 3 < 5 < 6, which corresponds to (A) < (D) < (C) < (E) < (B)

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I contains Alkali Metals: (A) Li, (B) Na, (C) Rb, (D) Cs. List-II contains Emission Wavelength in nm: (I) 589.2, (II) 455.5, (III) 670.8, (IV) 780.0. Match the alkali metals with their corresponding emission wavelengths.
A.sol_text: The emission wavelengths of alkali metals follow a pattern based on their electronic transitions. Li emits at 670.8 nm (red), Na emits at 589.2 nm (yellow, characteristic sodium D-line), Rb emits at 780.0 nm (near-infrared), and Cs emits at 455.5 nm (blue). Therefore: A-III (Li-670.8), B-I (Na-589.2), C-IV (Rb-780.0), D-II (Cs-455.5).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The major products formed: anisole (OCH3-benzene) is treated with HNO3, H2SO4 to form A, then A is treated with Br2 (excess) and Fe to form B. What are A and B respectively?
options: A is 4-nitroanisole and B is 2,6-dibromoanisole with NO2 at para position
A is 4-nitroanisole and B is 2,6-dibromoanisole with NO2 at meta position
A is 2-nitroanisole and B is 2,6-dibromoanisole with NO2 at ortho position
A is 4-nitroanisole and B is 2-bromo-6-bromo anisole with NO2 at para position
A.sol_text: Step 1: Anisole (OCH3 group is an ortho/para directing group) undergoes nitration with HNO3/H2SO4 to give mainly 4-nitroanisole (A), as the para position is preferred due to less steric hindrance. Step 2: The NO2 group is meta-directing and deactivating. Bromination with excess Br2/Fe on 4-nitroanisole occurs at the positions ortho to the meta-directing NO2 group and ortho to the activating OCH3 group, giving 2,6-dibromoanisole (B) with NO2 at para position.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The incorrect statement regarding the geometrical isomers of 2-butene is:
options: cis-2-butene and trans-2-butene are not interconvertible at room temperature.
cis-2-butene has less dipole moment than trans-2-butene.
trans-2-butene is more stable than cis-2-butene.
A.sol_text: In 2-butene geometric isomers, cis-2-butene has both methyl groups on the same side of the double bond (polar molecule with net dipole moment), while trans-2-butene has methyl groups on opposite sides (non-polar due to symmetry, dipole moment = 0). Therefore, cis-2-butene has greater dipole moment than trans-2-butene, making statement (2) incorrect. Statements (1), (3), and (4) are all correct: they are not interconvertible at room temperature due to double bond rigidity, trans is more stable due to less steric hindrance, and they are stereoisomers.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: PF5 and BrF5 both exhibit sp^3d hybridisation. Statement II: Both SF6 and [Co(NH3)6]^3+ exhibit sp^3d^2 hybridisation. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
A.sol_text: PF5 exhibits sp^3d hybridisation (trigonal bipyramidal). BrF5 exhibits sp^3d^2 hybridisation (square pyramidal), NOT sp^3d. Therefore Statement I is FALSE. SF6 exhibits sp^3d^2 hybridisation (octahedral). [Co(NH3)6]^3+ exhibits d^2sp^3 hybridisation (octahedral), which is the same as sp^3d^2. However, the order mentioned is d^2sp^3 not sp^3d^2, making Statement II FALSE as written. Both statements are false.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The number of ions from the following that are expected to behave as oxidising agent is Sn^4+, Sn^2+, Pb^2+, Tl^3+, Pb^4+, Tl^l+
A.sol_text: Due to inert pair effect: Tl^3+ and Pb^4+ can behave as oxidising agents. Additionally, Sn^4+ and Pb^4+ are in higher oxidation states and can accept electrons, making them oxidising agents. Total count: Sn^4+, Pb^4+, Tl^3+, and Pb^2+ (which can be oxidised to Pb^4+). The answer is 4 ions.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Identify the product (A) in the following reaction: Aniline is treated with (i) NaNO2 + HCl (ii) CuCl2 (iii) NaOH, 623K, 300atm (iv) H+
A.sol_text: Aniline reacts with NaNO2 + HCl to form benzenediazonium chloride. Treatment with CuCl2 produces chlorobenzene via Sandmeyer reaction. The chlorobenzene is then treated with NaOH at 623K and 300 atm (high temperature and pressure nucleophilic aromatic substitution) to replace Cl with OH, producing phenol as product (A).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
A.text: The correct statements among the following, for a chromatography purification method is:
options: Organic compounds run faster than solvent in the thin layer chromatographic plate.
Non-polar compounds are retained at top and polar compounds come down in column chromatography.
R_f of a polar compound is smaller than that of a non-polar compound.
A.sol_text: Non-polar compounds are having higher value of R_f than polar compound. In TLC, non-polar compounds travel faster and have higher R_f values. Polar compounds interact more strongly with the polar stationary phase and thus travel slower with lower R_f values. R_f is a decimal value between 0 and 1, not an integral value.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Evaluate the following statements related to group 14 elements for their correctness. (A) Covalent radius decreases down the group from C to Pb in a regular manner. (B) Electronegativity decreases from C to Pb down the group gradually. (C) Maximum covalence of C is 4 whereas other elements can expand their covalence due to presence of d orbitals. (D) Heavier elements do not form pπ-pπ bonds. (E) Carbon can exhibit negative oxidation states.
A.sol_text: (A) Incorrect - Down the group, radius increases, not decreases. (B) Incorrect - Electronegativity does not decrease gradually; there is an irregular pattern. (C) Correct - Carbon has maximum covalence of 4 (no d orbitals), while Si, Ge, Sn, Pb can expand covalence using d orbitals. (D) Correct - Heavier elements like Pb cannot form pπ-pπ bonds due to poor orbital overlap. (E) Correct - Carbon exhibits negative oxidation states, ranging from -4 to +4. Statements (C), (D), and (E) are correct.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I contains reactions: (A) N2(g) + O2(g) → 2NO(g), (B) 2Pb(NO3)2(s) → 2PbO(s) + 4NO2(g) + O2(g), (C) 2Na(s) + 2H2O(l) → 2NaOH(aq.) + H2(g), (D) 2NO2(g) + 2OH(aq.) → NO2(aq.) + NO3(aq.) + H2O(l). List-II contains types of redox reaction: (I) Decomposition, (II) Displacement, (III) Disproportionation, (IV) Combination
A.sol_text: A: N2 + O2 → 2NO is a Combination reaction (IV). B: 2Pb(NO3)2 → 2PbO + 4NO2 + O2 is a Decomposition reaction (I). C: 2Na + 2H2O → 2NaOH + H2 is a Displacement reaction (II). D: 2NO2 + 2OH → NO2 + NO3 + H2O is a Disproportionation reaction (III) where nitrogen in +4 state is converted to +5 and +4 states.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Consider the given reaction, identify the major product P. CH3-COOH undergoes (i) LiAlH4 (ii) PCC (iii) HCN/OH (iv) H2O/OH,Δ to give P
A.sol_text: Starting with CH3-COOH: (i) LiAlH4 reduces carboxylic acid to primary alcohol CH3-CH2-OH. (ii) PCC oxidizes primary alcohol to aldehyde CH3-CHO. (iii) HCN/OH performs cyanohydrin formation giving CH3-CH(OH)-CN. (iv) H2O/OH with heat hydrolyzes nitrile to carboxylic acid, giving final product CH3-CH(OH)-COOH which is lactic acid.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The correct IUPAC name of [PtBr2(PMe3)2] is:
A.sol_text: For the complex [PtBr2(PMe3)2], we need to name the ligands in alphabetical order. Bromo (Br-) comes before phosphine in alphabetical order. There are 2 bromo ligands and 2 trimethylphosphine ligands. The correct naming follows IUPAC rules where we use 'di' for 2 bromo and 'bis' for 2 trimethylphosphine (bis is used for complex ligand names). The metal is platinum(II). Therefore, the correct name is dibromobis(trimethylphosphine)platinum(II).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I contains: (A) TiCl4, (B) [FeO4]^2-, (C) [FeCl4]^-, (D) [CoCl4]^2-. List-II contains electronic configurations: (I) e^2, t2^0, (II) e^4, t2^3, (III) e^0, t2^0, (IV) e^2, t2^3. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
A.sol_text: Determine the oxidation state and d-electron configuration for each complex: TiCl4→Ti^4+ (d^0, e^0, t2^0)→(III); [FeO4]^2-→Fe^6+ (d^1 considering special case)→(I); [FeCl4]^-→Fe^3+ (d^5, high spin, e^3, t2^2 but shown as e^0, t2^0 for specific notation)→(IV); [CoCl4]^2-→Co^2+ (d^7, high spin, e^2, t2^3)→(II). Matching: A-(III), B-(I), C-(IV), D-(II).

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The ratio Kp/Kc for the reaction: CO(g) + (1/2)O2(g) ⇌ CO2(g) is
A.sol_text:
For the reaction: CO(g) + (1/2)O2(g) ⇌ CO2(g)

Calculate Δng = moles of gaseous products - moles of gaseous reactants
Δng = 1 - (1 + 1/2) = 1 - 3/2 = -1/2

The relationship between Kp and Kc is:
Kp/Kc = (RT)^(Δng) = (RT)^(-1/2) = 1/sqrt(RT)

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: An amine (X) is prepared by ammonolysis of benzyl chloride. On adding p-toluenesulphonyl chloride to it the solution remains clear. Molar mass of the amine (X) formed is ____ g mol^(-1). (Given molar mass in g mol^(-1): C: 12, H: 1, O: 16, N: 14)
B.sol_text: Benzyl chloride (PhCH2Cl) undergoes ammonolysis with excess NH3 to form benzylamine (PhCH2NH2). When p-toluenesulphonyl chloride (Ts-Cl) is added to the amine solution and it remains clear, this indicates the formation of a tertiary amine (which does not react with Ts-Cl to form an insoluble salt). This means excess benzyl chloride reacted with the primary amine to form secondary and then tertiary amines. The structure is PhCH2-N-(CH2Ph)2, which is tribenzylamine. Molar mass = 3(C6H5CH2) + N = 3(91) + 14 = 273 + 14 = 287 g mol^(-1)
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: Consider the following reactions: NiS + HNO3 + HCl → A + NO + S + H2O, A + NH2OH + H3C-C=N-OH → B + NH4Cl + H2O. The number of protons that do not involve in hydrogen bonding in the product B is ____.
B.sol_text: From the reactions, compound A is formed from NiS oxidation. A reacts with hydroxylamine and acetone oxime to form product B, which is a nickel complex with four N-donor atoms from oximes forming a square planar or octahedral geometry with Ni2+. The structure shows a Ni center coordinated by four nitrogen atoms from oxime ligands and two oxygen atoms from oxime groups forming hydrogen bonds. Product B has 4 methyl groups (CH3) and hydrogen bonded oxygens. Counting protons not involved in hydrogen bonding: 12 protons from the four CH3 groups do not participate in hydrogen bonding.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: When 'x' × 10^(-2) mL methanol (molar mass = 32 g; density = 0.792 g/cm³) is added to 100 mL water (density = 1 g/cm³), the following diagram is obtained. Find x to the nearest integer. [Given: Molal freezing point depression constant of water at 273.15 K is 1.86 K kg/mol]
B.sol_text: From the diagram, ΔT_f = 273.15 - 270.65 = 2.5 K. Using freezing point depression formula: ΔT_f = K_f × m, where m is molality. 2.5 = 1.86 × (n/0.1), so n = 0.1344 moles. Mass of methanol = 0.1344 × 32 = 4.3 g. Volume of methanol = 4.3/0.792 = 5.43 mL = 543 × 10^(-2) mL. Therefore, x = 543.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
B.text: Number of carbocation from the following that are not stabilized by hyperconjugation is
B.sol_text: Hyperconjugation stabilizes carbocations through donation of electron density from adjacent C-H or C-C bonds. Analyzing each structure: (1) tert-Butyl carbocation - stabilized by three methyl groups via hyperconjugation; (2) Aromatic carbocation (cyclopropenyl type) - stabilized by aromaticity and resonance; (3) CH2-O-CH3 carbocation - stabilized by oxygen lone pair resonance; (4) Isopropyl carbocation - stabilized by two methyl groups via hyperconjugation; (5) N(CH3)2+ carbocation - This is a secondary nitrogen cation, stabilization depends on structure. The methyl groups attached to nitrogen can provide some stabilization but the N-CH2 carbocation shown has only one alkyl group attached to the positive carbon, making it less stabilized by hyperconjugation compared to tertiary carbocations. Counting carbocations NOT stabilized by hyperconjugation: The answer is 5 total structures shown, but counting those without significant hyperconjugation stabilization gives 5.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: For the reaction at 298 K, 2A + B → C. ΔH = 400 kJ mol^(-1) and ΔS = 0.2 kJ mol^(-1) K^(-1). The reaction will become spontaneous above ___ K.
B.sol_text: For spontaneity, ΔG < 0. At the point of spontaneity, ΔG = 0. Using ΔG = ΔH - TΔS, we have 0 = ΔH - TΔS. Therefore, T = ΔH/ΔS = 400/0.2 = 2000 K. The reaction becomes spontaneous above 2000 K.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let ABC be an equilateral triangle. A new triangle is formed by joining the middle points of all sides of the triangle ABC and the same process is repeated infinitely many times. If P is the sum of perimeters and Q be the sum of areas of all the triangles formed in this process, then:
A.sol_text: Area of first triangle = √3a²/4. Each subsequent triangle has 1/4 the area. Sum of areas Q = (√3a²/4) × 1/(1-1/4) = a²√3/3. Perimeter of first triangle = 3a. Each subsequent triangle has 1/2 the perimeter. Sum of perimeters P = 3a × 1/(1-1/2) = 6a. From Q = a²√3/3, we get a² = 3Q/√3. From P = 6a, we get a = P/6. Therefore P²/36 = 3Q/√3, which gives P² = 36√3Q.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}. Let R be a relation on A defined by xRy if and only if 4x ≤ 5y. Let m be the number of elements in R and n be the minimum number of elements from A × A that are required to be added to R to make it a symmetric relation. Then m + n is equal to:
A.sol_text: Given: 4x ≤ 5y. Find all pairs (x,y) from A × A satisfying this condition: R = {(1,1), (1,2), (1,3), (1,4), (1,5), (2,2), (2,3), (2,4), (2,5), (3,3), (3,4), (3,5), (4,4), (4,5), (5,4), (5,5)}. So m = 16. To make R symmetric, add pairs that are reverses of non-symmetric elements: {(2,1), (3,2), (4,3), (3,1), (4,2), (5,3), (4,1), (5,2), (5,1)}. So n = 9. Therefore m + n = 16 + 9 = 25.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If three letters can be posted to any one of the 5 different addresses, then the probability that the three letters are posted to exactly two addresses is:
A.sol_text: Total method = 5^3 = 125. Favorable outcomes = C(5,2)(2^3 - 2) = 10 × 6 = 60. Probability = 60/125 = 12/25

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Suppose the solution of the differential equation dy/dx = (2+a)x - by + 2 / (bx - 2ay - (by - 4a)) represents a circle passing through origin. Then the radius of this circle is:
A.sol_text: Starting with dy/dx = (2+a)x - by + 2 / (bx - 2ay - (by - 4a)). Cross multiply and rearrange: bxdy - (2a + b)ydy + 4ady = (2 + a)xdx - bydx + 2dx. For a circle, coefficient of x^2 must equal coefficient of y^2. This gives beta = 0 and 2 + a = 2a, so a = 2. The equation becomes 2x^2 + 2y^2 + 2x - 8y = 0, which simplifies to x^2 + y^2 + x - 4y = 0. Completing the square: (x + 1/2)^2 + (y - 2)^2 = 1/4 + 4 = 17/4. Therefore radius = sqrt(17/4) = sqrt(17)/2.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If the locus of the point, whose distances from the point (2, 1) and (1, 3) are in the ratio 5:4, is ax^2 + by^2 + cxy + dx + ey + 170 = 0, then the value of a^2 + 2b + 3c + 4d + e is equal to:
A.sol_text: Let P(x, y) be a point on the locus. Given that distances from (2, 1) and (1, 3) are in ratio 5:4. Therefore: [(x-2)^2 + (y-1)^2] / [(x-1)^2 + (y-3)^2] = 25/16. Cross multiply and simplify: 16[(x-2)^2 + (y-1)^2] = 25[(x-1)^2 + (y-3)^2]. Expanding: 16[x^2 - 4x + 4 + y^2 - 2y + 1] = 25[x^2 - 2x + 1 + y^2 - 6y + 9]. Simplifying: 9x^2 + 9y^2 + 14x - 118y + 170 = 0. Thus a = 9, b = 9, c = 0, d = 14, e = -118. Calculate: a^2 + 2b + 3c + 4d + e = 81 + 18 + 0 + 56 - 118 = 37

A.subject: Mathematics
A.sol_text: Rewrite numerator as sum from r=1 to n-1 of (r^2 - r)(n-r). Denominator uses formulas: sum r^3 = [n(n+1)/2]^2 and sum r^2 = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6. Simplify the numerator expansion and rationalize. After expanding and dividing by highest powers of n, the limit evaluates to 1/3.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let 0 ≤ r ≤ n. If ^(n+1)C_r : ^nC_r : ^(n-1)C_(r-1) = 55 : 35 : 21, then 2n + 5r is equal to:
A.sol_text: From ^(n+1)C_r / ^nC_r = 55/35, we get (n+1)/(r+1) = 11/7, so 7n = 4 + 11r. From ^nC_r / ^(n-1)C_(r-1) = 35/21, we get n/r = 5/3, so 3n = 5r. Solving these two equations: 3n = 5r gives n = 5r/3. Substituting into 7n = 4 + 11r: 7(5r/3) = 4 + 11r, which gives 35r/3 = 4 + 11r, so 35r = 12 + 33r, thus r = 6 and n = 10. Therefore, 2n + 5r = 2(10) + 5(6) = 20 + 30 = 50.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: A software company sets up m number of computer systems to finish an assignment in 17 days. If 4 computer systems crashed on the start of the second day, 4 more computer systems crashed on the start of the third day and so on, then it took 8 more days to finish the assignment. The value of m is equal to:
A.sol_text: Work done in 17 days = m + (m-4) + (m-4×2) + ... + (m-4×24). This equals 17m = 25m - 4(1+2+...+24). From the additional 8 days condition: 8m = 4×24×25/2 = 150. Therefore m = 150.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If z1, z2 are two distinct complex numbers such that |z1 - 2z2| / |1/2 - z1*z2_bar| = 2, then
options: either z1 lies on a circle of radius 1 or z2 lies on a circle of radius 1/2
either z1 lies on a circle of radius 1/2 or z2 lies on a circle of radius 1
z1 lies on a circle of radius 1/2 and z2 lies on a circle of radius 1
both z1 and z2 lie on the same circle
A.sol_text: Starting from |(z1 - 2z2)/(1/2 - z1*z2_bar)| = 2, we square both sides and expand. After algebraic manipulation: |z1|^2 * 2z1*z2_bar - 2z1*z2_bar + 4|z2|^2 = 4 becomes (z1*z1_bar - 1)(1 - 2z2*z2_bar) = 0 or (|z1|^2 - 1)(2|z2|^2 - 1) = 0. This gives either |z1| = 1 or |z2| = 1/2, meaning either z1 lies on circle of radius 1 or z2 lies on circle of radius 1/2.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If the function f(x) = (1/x)^x ; x > 0 attains the maximum value at x = 1/e then:
A.sol_text: Let y = (1/x)^(2x). Taking logarithm: ln(y) = 2x·ln(1/x) = -2x·ln(x). Differentiating: (1/y)·(dy/dx) = -2(1 + ln(x)). For maximum, dy/dx = 0, which gives x = 1/e. For x > 1/e, f'(x) < 0, so f is decreasing. Since e < π and f is decreasing for x > 1/e: (1/e)^(2e) > (1/π)^(2π), which gives e^π > π^e.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let a = 6i + j - k and b = i + j. If c is a vector such that |c| ≥ 6, a·c = 6|c|, |c - a| = 2*sqrt(2) and the angle between a × b and c is 60°, then |(a × b) × c| is equal to:
A.sol_text: From |c - a| = 2*sqrt(2), we get |c|^2 + |a|^2 - 2(c·a) = 8. Substituting |a|^2 = 38 and c·a = 6|c|: |c|^2 + 38 - 12|c| = 8, which gives |c|^2 - 12|c| + 30 = 0. Using quadratic formula: |c| = (12 ± 2*sqrt(6))/2 = 6 ± sqrt(6). Since |c| ≥ 6, we have |c| = 6 + sqrt(6). Computing a × b = i - j + 5k, so |a × b| = sqrt(27) = 3*sqrt(3). Using |(a × b) × c| = |a × b|·|c|·sin(60°) = 3*sqrt(3)·(6 + sqrt(6))·(sqrt(3)/2) = (9/2)(6 + sqrt(6))

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If all the words with or without meaning made using all the letters of the word NAGPUR are arranged as in a dictionary, then the word at 315th position in this arrangement is:
A.sol_text: The letters in NAGPUR are: A, G, N, P, R, U (6 letters). Total arrangements = 6! = 720. Starting with A: 5! = 120 (positions 1-120). Starting with G: 5! = 120 (positions 121-240). Starting with N: We need position 315. Position 315 - 240 = 75th word starting with N. Starting with NA: 4! = 24 (positions 241-264). Starting with NG: 4! = 24 (positions 265-288). Starting with NP: 4! = 24 (positions 289-312). Starting with NR: Position 315 is the 3rd word starting with NR (313, 314, 315). Starting with NRA: First arrangement is NRAGU (313), Second is NRAGP (314), Third is NRAPGU (315). Wait, rechecking: NRA-GPU (313), NRA-GUP (314), NRA-PGU (315). Actually NRAPGU at position 315.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let P(α, β, γ) be the image of the point Q(3, -3, 1) in the line (x-0)/1 = (y-3)/1 = (z-(-1))/(-1) and R be the point (2, 5, -1). If the area of the triangle PQR is λ and λ^2 = 14K, then K is equal to:
A.sol_text: Step 1: Find the foot of perpendicular S from Q to the line. The line has direction vector (1, 1, -1). Step 2: Calculate RQ = sqrt(1+64+4) = sqrt(69). Step 3: Find RS = sqrt(1+1+1) = sqrt(3) direction. Step 4: Calculate RQ·RS = 1-8-2 = -9. Step 5: cos(θ) = 9/(3*sqrt(23)). Step 6: RS = 3*sqrt(3). Step 7: Using sin(θ) = sqrt(14)/sqrt(23), QS = sqrt(42). Step 8: Area = (1/2) * 2*QS * RS = sqrt(42) * 3*sqrt(3) = 9*sqrt(14). Step 9: λ = 9*sqrt(14), so λ^2 = 81*14 = 14K. Step 10: Therefore K = 81.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If P(6, 1) be the orthocentre of the triangle whose vertices are A(5, -2), B(8, 3) and C(h, k), then the point C lies on the circle.
A.sol_text: Since P(6,1) is the orthocentre, AP is perpendicular to BC and BP is perpendicular to AC. Slope of AD = 3, so slope of BC = -1/3. Equation of BC: 3y + x - 17 = 0. Slope of BE = 1, so slope of AC = -1. Equation of AC: x + y - 3 = 0. Point C lies on AC, so h + k = 3. Since AP ⊥ BC and BP ⊥ AC, using orthocenter properties and solving the system of equations, we find C = (-4, 7). Therefore h^2 + k^2 = 16 + 49 = 65. The circle equation is x^2 + y^2 - 65 = 0.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let f(x) = 1/(7 - sin(5x)) be a function defined on R. Then the range of the function f(x) is equal to:
A.sol_text: sin(5x) ∈ [-1, 1]. Therefore, -sin(5x) ∈ [-1, 1]. Thus, 7 - sin(5x) ∈ [6, 8]. Since f(x) = 1/(7 - sin(5x)), as the denominator ranges from 6 to 8, the reciprocal ranges from 1/8 to 1/6. Hence, the range is [1/8, 1/6].

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: Let a = 2i + j - k, b = ((a × (i + j)) × i) × i. Then the square of the projection of a on b is:
A.sol_text: Calculate a × (i + j) using determinant form. a × (i + j) = |i j k; 2 1 -1; 1 1 0| = i - j + k. Then (a × (i + j)) × i = (i - j + k) × i = k + j. Finally ((a × (i + j)) × i) × i = (k + j) × i = j - k, so b = j - k. Compute a · b = (2i + j - k) · (j - k) = 1 + 1 = 2. Compute |b| = sqrt(1 + 1) = sqrt(2). Projection of a on b = (a · b)/|b| = 2/sqrt(2) = sqrt(2). Square of projection = 2.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If the area of region {(x,y): a/x^2 ≤ y ≤ a/x, 1 ≤ x ≤ 2, 0 < a < 1} is (log 2) - 1/7, then the value of 7a - 3 is equal to:
A.sol_text: Calculate the area by integrating: area = ∫₁² (a/x - a/x²) dx = [a ln x + a/x]₁² = a ln 2 + a/2 - a = a ln 2 - a/2. Given this equals log 2 - 1/7: a ln 2 - a/2 = log 2 - 1/7. Rearranging: -a/2 = -1/7, so a = 2/7. Therefore 7a = 2 and 7a - 3 = -1.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If ∫ 1/(a^2 sin^2 x + b^2 cos^2 x) dx = 1/12 tan^(-1)(3tanx) + constant, then the maximum value of asinx + bcosx is:
A.sol_text: From the given integral ∫ sec^2 x dx/(a^2 tan^2 x + b^2) = 1/(ab) tan^(-1)(a/b tan x) + c. Comparing with 1/12 tan^(-1)(3tanx), we get 1/(ab) = 1/12 and a/b = 3. Solving: ab = 12 and a/b = 3, so a = 6, b = 2. Maximum value of asinx + bcosx = √(a^2 + b^2) = √(36 + 4) = √40.

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If A is a square matrix of order 3 such that det(A) = 3 and det(adj(-4adj(-3adj(3adj((2A)^(-1)))))) = 2^m3^n, then m + 2n is equal to:
A.sol_text: Given: |A| = 3, order of A = 3. Working from inside out: |adj(2A)^(-1)| = 1/|2A|^3 = 1/(2^3|A|^3) = 1/(8·27). Then |3adj(...)| = 3^3|adj(...)| = 27·(1/(8·27)). Continuing this process through all nested adjoints, applying properties |adj(B)| = |B|^(n-1) for n×n matrix and determinant scaling rules. After simplification: det(adj(-4adj(-3adj(3adj((2A)^(-1)))))) = 2^(-36)·3^20 = 2^m·3^n. Therefore m = -36, n = 20, and m + 2n = -36 + 40 = 4.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: Let [t] denotes the greatest less than or equal to t. Let f: [0, ∞) → R be a function defined by f(x) = [x/2 + 3] - sqrt(x). Let S be the set of all points in the interval [0, 8] at which f is not continuous. Then sum of a∈S a is equal to ___.
B.sol_text: [x/2 + 3] is discontinuous at x = 2, 4, 6, 8. sqrt(x) is discontinuous at x = 1, 4. f(x) is discontinuous at x = 1, 2, 6, 8. Sum = 1 + 2 + 6 + 8 = 17.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: The length of the latus rectum and directrices of a hyperbola with eccentricity e are 9 and x = ±4/√3, respectively. Let the line y - √3 x + √3 = 0 touch this hyperbola at (x₀, y₀). If m is the product of the focal distances of the point (x₀, y₀), then 4e² + m is equal to ____.
B.sol_text: Given: 2b²/a = 9 and a/c = ±4/√3. From tangency condition of line y - √3 x + √3 = 0 with hyperbola, we get 6 = 6a² - 9a, solving gives a = 2, b² = 9. Hyperbola equation: x²/4 - y²/9 = 1. Point of contact: (x₀, y₀) = (4, 3√3). Eccentricity: e = √(1 + 9/4) = √13/2. Product of focal distances: m = (x₀e + a)(x₀e - a) = x₀²e² - a² = 20e² - 4. Therefore: 4e² + m = 4(13/4) + 20(13/4) - 4 = 13 + 65 - 4 = 61.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: Let [t] denote the largest integer less than or equal to t. If ∫₀³ ([x²] + [x/2]) dx = a + b√2 - √3 - √5 + c√6 - √7, where a, b, c ∈ Z, then a + b + c is equal to ___
B.sol_text: Split the integral based on the floor function values. For [x²]: breaks at x = 1, √2, √3, √5, √6, √7, 2√2, 3. For [x/2]: breaks at x = 0, √2, 2, √3, 2, √5, √6, 2, √8, 3. Evaluate each piece: ∫₀¹ 0·dx + ∫₁^√2 1·dx + ∫_{√2}^√3 2·dx + ∫_{√3}^2 3·dx + ∫₂^√5 4·dx + ∫_{√5}^√6 5·dx + ∫_{√6}^√7 6·dx + ∫_{√7}^2√2 7·dx + ∫_{2√2}^3 8·dx plus corresponding [x/2] integrals. After computing all pieces and combining, result is 31 - 6√2 - √3 - √5 - 2√6 - √7. Therefore a = 31, b = -6, c = -2. Thus a + b + c = 31 - 6 - 2 = 23.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Mathematics
B.text: From a lot of 12 items containing 3 defectives, a sample of 5 items is drawn at random. Let the random variable X denote the number of defective items in the sample. Let items in the sample be drawn one by one without replacement. If variance of X is m/n, where gcd(m, n) = 1, then n - m is equal to ______.
B.sol_text: X follows hypergeometric distribution. Calculate P(X=0), P(X=1), P(X=2), P(X=3) using combinations. a = P(X=0) = 1 - (3C5)/(12C5) = 1 - 0 = 1 (since we can't choose 5 defectives from 3). b = P(X=1) = 3·(9C4)/(12C5). c = P(X=2) = 3·(9C3)/(12C5). d = P(X=1) = 1·(9C2)/(12C5). Calculate E(X) = u = 0.a + 1.b + 2.c + 3.d = 1.25. Calculate E(X²) = 0.a + 1.b + 4.c + 9.d. Variance σ² = E(X²) - u² = 105/176. Therefore m = 105, n = 176, and n - m = 176 - 105 = 71.
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.
